name: Mind Placed Inside the Skull
previous_label: Virabhadrasana II — Warrior II (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: kapālāntar mano nyasya tiṣṭhan mīlitalocanaḥ | krameṇa manaso dārḍhyāl lakṣayel lakṣyam uttamam ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
sanskrit_variants: GRETIL e-text prints dārḍhyāt lakṣayet laṣyam (unsandhied forms plus a typo for lakṣyam).
dharana.rendering: Remaining with eyes closed, place the mind inside the skull; as steadiness of mind gradually grows, one perceives the highest thing to be perceived.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: 'tiṣṭhan' means remaining or abiding; Singh renders it 'seated', Bäumer 'sitting motionless', Silburn 'se tenant', Wallis 'remaining'. Satsangi locates the attention at the crown of the head and The Mystery Within glosses the place as the sahasrāra cakra; most translators say 'inside the cranium'. Singh also records an esoteric reading of kapāla as the union of Śiva and Śakti.

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y8 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)
numbering_variants.hatha_es: dharana 11 = verse 106 (connection of subject and object); non-standard, not followed (the previous draft of this door followed it)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 34 does not prescribe a body position (it specifies closed eyes and uses the verb tiṣṭhan, 'remaining', which Singh renders 'seated'). The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the inner space of the skull (kapāla)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the bowl of space inside the skull, held as a soft field rather than a tight point. Closed eyes are part of the verse; posture is not specified.
geometry.svg_hint: an outline of the head with a soft glow filling the inner space, eyes drawn closed
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Gather to stillness
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: scattered mental effort gathers into one steady field inside the skull, steadiness building bit by bit.

breath.lands_in: soft, even breath; no bracing in the throat
breath.cue: Natural, even breath, about four in and four out. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention inward to the space inside the skull
orientation.gravity: Body supported and still; head balanced without effort
orientation.gaze: Eyes closed (the verse specifies closed eyes)
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The steady space inside the skull, held as a soft field
attention.secondary: Steadiness growing gradually, without forcing a vision or a blank

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Remaining with eyes closed, place the mind inside the skull; as steadiness of mind gradually grows, one perceives the highest thing to be perceived.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sit or lie quietly, close the eyes, and place attention inside the skull as a soft field rather than a clenched point. Let mental steadiness build bit by bit without forcing a vision or a blank.

honesty.disclosure: Door 011 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 11 (verse 34) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 011 is dharana 11, verse 34. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.
Numbering correction: the previous draft of this door followed hatha.es's non-standard numbering (dharana 11 = verse 106 (connection of subject and object)). Rebuilt to Singh's verse 34.
Content moved: the previous Door 008 draft carried verse 34. It now lives here, at its Singh position.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture]↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. [retired posture] and VBT dharana 011 are paired by school index for teaching, not as a historical one-to-one.
legacy.notes: Soft experiential resonance only: the [retired posture]’s dual reach and forward gaze make the ‘connection of seeing’ easy to point to in class. That does not upgrade the pairing beyond school_device.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If attention in the head brings pressure or a headache, move attention down to the breath at the belly or open the eyes and stop. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Shorten stance or reduce front-knee bend if knees, hips, or shoulders complain. Do not force the front thigh parallel or square the pelvis past what keeps the front knee tracking.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 011: mind placed inside the skull. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 11, verse 34.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie in any steady way. The map is the bowl of space inside the head.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body still and supported, head balanced. Close the eyes: the verse asks for that.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural, even breath, four in and four out. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Rest attention inside the skull as a soft field. Let steadiness grow by itself.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: scattered effort gathers into one steady field. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 34: with eyes closed, place the mind inside the skull; as it steadies, one perceives the highest thing to be perceived. Do not force a vision or a blank.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let attention drop to the breath at the belly. Open the eyes slowly.
